what_it_does: Smartphone displays refresh at a fixed rhythm (called VSync, for vertical sync) — typically 60 or 120 times per second — and the phone's GPU (the graphics chip) is traditionally locked to finish drawing each frame within that exact window. On large, high-refresh-rate screens with complex animations, this fixed deadline is increasingly hard to meet: if the GPU needs just a little longer, the frame is dropped entirely, causing a visible stutter. D-VSync decouples the drawing pipeline from the display rhythm by letting the GPU finish a frame whenever it is ready, while a new buffering and synchronization layer holds the finished frame and presents it at the nearest available display opportunity. A predictive scheduler anticipates how long each frame will take and aligns work accordingly, reducing the number of missed display windows.
